description: The FSF sample research (DECISIONS D-059), shown in the practice space. Fictional: the research, numbers, code, pictures, DOIs and people are made up to show what the app does. records.zh.json holds the same steps in Chinese; files/ is made by tools/make_fsf_sample.py.

steps.title: Intuition: flow speed levels off
steps.body:
An old notebook page, photographed and added today.

Hunch: when the forcing rises, the flow speed does not grow without bound — it levels off. Why, and how fast?
steps.author_statement: Written in a paper notebook in September 2025.

steps.title: Reading notes: three earlier models
steps.body:
# Reading notes

- **Model A** — linear response; no saturation at all.
- **Model B** — logistic saturation with a fixed exponent.
- **Model C** — an empirical fit, no mechanism.

None of them lets the exponent change with the forcing.

steps.title: Seminar question: is the exponent really fixed?
steps.body: A colleague asked whether the saturation exponent could change with the forcing. No answer yet — worth checking.

steps.title: Code history before recording started: Oct–Nov 2025 (5 commits)
steps.body:
Commits on main before this repository was recorded:

- 1c8e2f0 Start notebook port of the flow model
- 4b07a93 Add plotting helpers

- b2f9c41 Fix units in the output
- 9e41f07 Clean up before the prototype
steps.author_statement: Added when recording from git began; the dates are what git says.

steps.title: Hypothesis H1: saturation follows a power law
steps.body: H1: v approaches 1 as (1 − v)^α with a fixed exponent α = 1.5.

steps.title: Formula v1
steps.body:
dv/dt = k (1 - v)^alpha

with k = 0.8 and alpha = 1.5 (from H1).

steps.title: Solver prototype
steps.body: Prototype solver for formula v1: explicit Euler, fixed step.
steps.author_statement: Recorded from git, with a copy of the code at this commit.

steps.title: Numerical experiment 1
steps.body:
# Run 1

Solver prototype, k = 0.8, α = 1.5, 80 steps.

Result: it converges, but the fitted exponent is about **1.3**, not 1.5.

steps.title: Figure 1: saturation curve
steps.body: v(t) from run 1. The curve flattens more slowly than H1 predicts.

steps.title: Hypothesis H1′: the exponent depends on the forcing
steps.body: H1′: α is not fixed; it falls as the forcing F rises.
steps.author_statement: Run 1 contradicted the fixed exponent, and the seminar question pointed the same way, so the hypothesis changed.

steps.title: Side idea: a lattice model
steps.body: Instead of the equation, try a lattice discretisation of the channel. It might explain the changing exponent directly.

steps.title: Lattice model test run
steps.body: 64 × 64 grid. The exponent comes out at 1.1 — suspiciously low.

steps.title: Formula v2
steps.body:
dv/dt = k (1 - v)^alpha(F)

alpha(F) = 1.5 - 0.2 F

steps.title: Solver v2: the exponent follows the forcing
steps.body: alpha_of(F) = 1.5 - 0.2 F; solve() takes the forcing level.

steps.title: Fix: adaptive step size (tag v0.2)
steps.body:
The fixed Euler step was too large near v = 1; the step now adapts.

Tagged v0.2.

steps.title: Numerical experiment 2: three forcing levels
steps.body:
# Run 2

Solver v0.2 with formula v2 at F = 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5.

The residual drops from 0.041 (formula v1) to 0.012.

steps.title: Figure 2: exponent versus forcing
steps.body: The fitted α at three forcing levels, with the line α(F) = 1.5 − 0.2 F.

steps.title: Meeting with the advisor
steps.body:
- Check the boundary condition in the lattice model.
- Compare with Model C on the same data.
- Run a sensitivity sweep before writing anything up.

steps.title: Experiment 3: sensitivity sweep
steps.body: Swept k from 0.6 to 1.0 and F from 0.25 to 2.0 — 35 runs. α(F) stays linear to within ±0.03.

steps.title: Result: α falls linearly with the forcing (0.25 ≤ F ≤ 2)
steps.body: Within 0.25 ≤ F ≤ 2, α(F) = 1.5 − 0.2 F fits every run to within 0.03.

steps.title: Paper draft v2, after the advisor's comments
steps.author_statement: Rewrote the method section after the meeting: the lattice part is gone, the sweep is in.

steps.title: Preprint: forcing-dependent saturation of flow speed
steps.body: Archived as a preprint.
steps.author_statement: The DOI is the strongest outside reference for when the paper existed. (In this sample the DOI is made up and does not open.)

steps.title: Reviewer questions
steps.body:
1. Is the linear α(F) an artefact of the step size?
2. What happens above F = 2?

steps.title: Experiment 4: robustness check for the reviewer
steps.body: Halved and doubled the step size: α(F) changes by less than 0.005. Above F = 2 the solver becomes unstable.

steps.title: Preprint v2 (revised)
steps.body: Answers both reviewer questions; the range of the result is stated as 0.25 ≤ F ≤ 2.

steps.title: Next question: what happens above F = 2?
steps.body: The solver becomes unstable there. A different method, or a different regime of the flow?

steps.title: Flow channel: the setup
steps.body: Acrylic channel, 1.2 m long. The pump runs on a variable-frequency controller (0–50 Hz); a flow sensor sits at the outlet.

steps.title: Calibration procedure
steps.body:
1. Let the pump run 10 minutes.
2. Step the controller from 10 to 50 Hz.
3. Read the flow sensor at each step, three times.

steps.statement: Noticed later: Figure 2 also re-plots the run 1 data as a baseline.
The lattice model was dropped, so the method no longer builds on it.

Every result in the preprint was computed with this version (tag v0.2).
